issues.body: The dispatch branch emits `type=raw,value=${{ needs.setup.outputs.version }}` and `setup.outputs.version` is the unconstrained required `inputs.tag`. Therefore a manual dispatch with `tag=latest` still pushes `:latest`; values such as `1.2` or an existing release version can likewise overwrite canonical tags. This contradicts the new comments and the load-bearing guarantee that developer/test dispatches cannot claim a tag followed by deployments. The structural test only proves the explicit canonical tag entries are gated; it never validates the effective dispatch tag set for adversarial/colliding input.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the dispatch input before any publishing jobs run and reject reserved/canonical forms (at minimum `latest`, stable semver tags, and moving major.minor tags), or namespace dispatch images unconditionally (for example `dev-${resolved/sanitized-version}`) so user input cannot equal a canonical tag. Extend `scripts/tests/test_release_container_multiarch.py` to pin that validation/namespace and include mutation or fixture cases for `latest` and a stable semver/major.minor collision.
issues.title: Manual dispatch can still overwrite canonical container tags

verdict.summary: The trigger gating removes the explicit `latest` tag on manual dispatch, but it does not enforce the claimed safety property because the dispatch-provided version is copied into a raw image tag without validation. A caller can supply `latest`, `1.2`, or another canonical/moving tag and overwrite exactly the deployment-followed tag this change intends to protect. The added contract test only checks YAML strings and therefore passes despite this semantic hole.
